judgments.comparative_verdict: Both reports hit every expectation with equivalent grounding and citations; they are comparable.

report_1.evidence: failures began at 14:03 and the first alert fired at 14:50 — a **47-minute detection gap**, not "minutes."

report_2.evidence: checkout failures began at 14:03 and the first alert fired at 14:50 — a 47-minute detection gap.

report_1.evidence: "During the window 1,284 transactions failed and required manual reprocessing; 37 were unrecoverable and refunded."

report_2.evidence: records that 1,284 transactions failed and required manual reprocessing, and 37 were unrecoverable and refunded.

report_1.evidence: `larkpay-comms/docs/sla-commitments.md` states the contractual monthly SLA is 99.9% ... April 2026 was 99.77% (`larkpay-comms/metrics/uptime-2026.csv`, line 6) — a breach.

report_2.evidence: `larkpay-comms/metrics/uptime-2026.csv` (line 6) shows April 2026 at 99.77%, below the 99.9% contractual monthly SLA in `larkpay-comms/docs/sla-commitments.md`, which states that any month below 99.9% "is a breach and owes service credits."

report_1.evidence: This violates rule 1 of `larkpay-comms/docs/customer-comms-style-guide.md` ("Never assign blame to an individual").

report_2.evidence: `larkpay-comms/docs/customer-comms-style-guide.md` rule 1 says "Never assign blame to an individual."

report_1.evidence: Rule 3 of `larkpay-comms/docs/customer-comms-style-guide.md` requires leading with impact and remediation. The draft instead opens with a (false) uptime boast ... and buries the sole remediation ... in the final line

report_2.evidence: Rule 3 of `larkpay-comms/docs/customer-comms-style-guide.md` requires leading with impact and remediation, but the draft opens with an uptime boast (lines 3–4) and closes with marketing language ... burying impact (misstated) and remediation (single last line, line 21).
